reason: Both cover the folate core, histidine/neural-tube, methionine cycle, nucleotide synthesis, selenium and cobalamin/B-vitamin contexts, but A adds several overlapping methionine-salvage variants plus more distal polyamine, choline and glutathione themes, so B gives the same one-carbon facets with much less redundancy.

Both span severing/capping, leading-edge ruffles and lamellipodia, filopodia/EPHB, focal-adhesion IPP, macropinocytosis/podosomes and Rho GTPase signalling, but A spreads these over 27 heavily overlapping themes while B gives the same facets in about half as many.

B keeps the relevant smooth-muscle contraction, relaxin/reproductive-behaviour and tachykinin contexts in a compact set, whereas A adds repeated GI-motility variants and off-target vascular blood-pressure and aminergic-receptor themes that do little to explain uterine contraction at parturition.

Both place the target in FOXO regulation, IGF/apoptosis, glycolytic/p53-mTOR metabolism, NRF2, HSF1 and ER/mitochondrial stress, but B repeats these as many near-identical FOXO-NRF2-metabolism blends, and its only real gain (a small cell-cycle/G0 theme) does not justify the clutter.

B adds a clean HIV transcription-initiation level and a coherent HIV life-cycle/host-restriction theme (integration, latency, APOBEC3G, retroelement silencing) that A lacks, giving the viral-infection facet alongside the Pol II elongation and Pol I/III transcription contexts, at the cost of some overlapping Pol II themes.

A covers neutrophil degranulation/respiratory burst, antimicrobial peptides/defensins, macrophage/CGD and complement in 14 well-separated themes, while B fragments the antimicrobial-peptide and metal-sequestration context into many near-duplicate themes and adds only modest formyl-peptide and Mtb-evasion facets.
